# What Langfuse secret keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# A key is the prefix sk-lf- and a UUID, forty-two characters in all. The bodies
# here are the ordered run 0123456789abcdef written twice over with the
# separators a UUID puts through it, 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef, which
# no real credential is. It is spelled in lowercase where the case does not
# matter and in uppercase where the case is what a case is about: the
# hexadecimal is read in either.
#
# Four cases carry a body that is not that run, because what each of them turns
# on is a body the run cannot state. The three version cases write the version
# and variant characters of the UUID they are about, and the placeholder is one
# repeated digit.

patterns: langfuse-secret-key

# Where a key is written. Langfuse issues a public key and a secret key together
# and the two authenticate as one, so the places a secret key stands are mostly
# places the public key stands beside it.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=«langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a key exported from a dotenv file
in:       export LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY="sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef"
out:      export LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY="«langfuse-secret-key»"

case:     a key passed to the client the SDK guides initialize
in:       Langfuse(public_key="pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef", secret_key="sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef")
out:      Langfuse(public_key="pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef", secret_key="«langfuse-secret-key»")

case:     a key on the command line the public API docs print
in:       curl -u pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef:sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/projects
out:      curl -u pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef:«langfuse-secret-key» https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/projects

case:     a key in json
in:       {"publicKey":"pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef","secretKey":"sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef"}
out:      {"publicKey":"pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef","secretKey":"«langfuse-secret-key»"}

case:     a key in yaml
in:       langfuse:\n  secret_key: sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      langfuse:\n  secret_key: «langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a key in a container environment
in:       docker run -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef app
out:      docker run -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=«langfuse-secret-key» app

case:     a key in a diff line
in:       +LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      +LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=«langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a key in a markdown code span
in:       set `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef` before running
out:      set `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=«langfuse-secret-key»` before running

case:     a key in a log line
in:       time=2026-09-14T00:00:00Z level=error msg="ingestion rejected" key=sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      time=2026-09-14T00:00:00Z level=error msg="ingestion rejected" key=«langfuse-secret-key»

# The alphabet the five groups are written in. Langfuse writes these lowercase
# and the hexadecimal is read in either case, so what the wider reading admits
# is a shape nobody issues rather than a key left in the text.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89AB-CDEF-0123-456789ABCDEF
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a body opening on the last lowercase letter hexadecimal admits
in:       sk-lf-f1234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a body closing on the last digit
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcde9
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

case:     the letter above hexadecimal where a body opens
in:       sk-lf-g1234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      sk-lf-g1234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     the letter above hexadecimal where a body closes
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdeg
out:      sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdeg

case:     an underscore in the body
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab_cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      sk-lf-01234567-89ab_cdef-0123-456789abcdef

# The layout. A UUID's four separators stand at fixed places, and that is the
# whole of what tells a body from thirty-six other characters written behind the
# prefix, so the count is read exactly rather than as a floor.

case:     a body one character short of the layout
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcde
out:      sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcde

case:     a separator missing from the body
in:       sk-lf-01234567089ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      sk-lf-01234567089ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a separator where the body carries a hexadecimal digit
in:       sk-lf-0123456--89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      sk-lf-0123456--89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a hexadecimal run longer than the layout is a key and what follows it
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef0
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»0

# The version of the UUID is not read. Langfuse mints a key from a version 4
# UUID, which writes a 4 at the first character of the third group and one of 8,
# 9, a and b at the first of the fourth; a scan reading those two characters
# would locate nothing at all were Langfuse to change generators.

case:     a body langfuse would mint today
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-4def-8123-456789abcdef
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a body of another version
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-7def-9123-456789abcdef
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a body whose version is version 4's and whose variant is not
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-4def-c123-456789abcdef
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

# The prefix is read as Langfuse writes it, and it is the whole of the anchor.

case:     the prefix written in capitals
in:       SK-LF-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      SK-LF-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     underscores where the prefix carries its hyphens
in:       sk_lf_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      sk_lf_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a run of the right shape opening with no prefix
in:       01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

# Nothing is asked of the character either side of a key. A demand in front
# would drop the key a word character is written against rather than trim it,
# and the count being exact is what leaves whatever follows a key in the text.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY_sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY_«langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xsk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      x«langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdefsuffix
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»suffix

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef-suffix
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»-suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef.
out:      the key is «langfuse-secret-key».

case:     a key immediately against japanese on both sides
in:       日本語sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef日本語
out:      日本語«langfuse-secret-key»日本語

case:     a key against an invalid byte
in:       \xffsk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      \xff«langfuse-secret-key»

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdefsk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»«langfuse-secret-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      «langfuse-secret-key» «langfuse-secret-key»

# The public key, which Langfuse publishes by design: its browser SDK takes that
# key and nothing else, and its docs write it into a name Next.js compiles into
# what the browser downloads. Redacting it would take an identifier out of a log
# rather than a credential.

case:     a public key
in:       pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a public key in an environment assignment
in:       LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

# What the grammar takes on, and what it declines to be anchored on. A
# placeholder written behind the prefix is a key's format character for
# character and is redacted; a UUID with nothing in front of it is what a trace
# id and a request id are written as, and reading one would redact those
# wherever a log line carries them.

case:     a placeholder uuid written behind the prefix
in:       LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
out:      LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=«langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a uuid as a trace id
in:       trace_id=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      trace_id=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     an iso timestamp in a log line
in:       time=2026-09-14T00:00:00Z level=info msg="flushing trace batch" events=12
out:      time=2026-09-14T00:00:00Z level=info msg="flushing trace batch" events=12

case:     a git sha
in:       commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
